test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Amit had invested the same amount of sums at simple as well as compound interest, compounded annually. The time period of investment for both the sums was 2 years and rate of interest too was same, 4% per annum. At the end, he found a difference of ₹44 in both the interests received. What were the sums (in ₹) invested?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a period of **2 years**, the difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** is given by the formula: **Difference = P × (R/100)²**.

Given **Difference** = ₹44 and **Rate (R)** = 4%.

⇒ 44 = P × (4/100)²

⇒ 44 = P × (1/25)² ⇒ 44 = P ÷ 625

⇒ P = 44 × 625 = ₹27,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Rate (R)** = 4% per annum

**Difference (CI − SI)** = ₹44

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Compound Interest (CI) = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d99ce0a5aa2501768983449bd0a1c162a3850e9ced74654e60a9e94c380522c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Principal** be P.

⇒ SI = (P × 4 × 2) ÷ 100 = 0.08P

⇒ CI = P[(1 + 4/100)² − 1]

⇒ CI = P[(1.04)² − 1] = P[1.0816 − 1] = 0.0816P

⇒ Difference = CI − SI = 0.0816P − 0.08P = 0.0016P

⇒ 0.0016P = 44

⇒ P = 44 ÷ 0.0016 = 440,000 ÷ 16

⇒ P = ₹27,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is given by: Difference = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years at R%, the effective CI rate is (R + R + R²/100)%, while the SI rate is simply (2R)%.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate the time to double an investment: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Interest Rate.
